# Frozen index-key encodings of numbers. The key bytes are a persisted format:
# they were produced by the encoder that wrote keys in released versions and
# must never be regenerated from the current code. A mismatch means keys
# already on disk would no longer be found.
#
# The two decoded columns are the decode contract, not a recording of released
# output: a key reads back as a Decimal when it is zero or between a millionth
# and 2^96, rounded to what a Decimal holds, and otherwise as the nearest float;
# read as a float or a decimal by its own kind it is the float its digits denote
# or the exact Decimal of them, whatever the magnitude.
#
# <value> <key bytes, hex> <decoded, index format> <decoded, own kind>
#   value:   i:<i64> | d:<mantissa>:<scale> | f:<f64 bits, hex>
#   decoded: i:<i64> | d:<mantissa>:<scale> | f:<f64 bits, hex> | err
#
# The floats include every other binary exponent, values whose digits differ
# from the exactly rounded expansion, and random bit patterns; the decimals
# include small values that decode through the float fallback.
